section: Elements and factors of climate; world climatic classification (Koeppen)
subsections: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

accepted.s: Who proposed the empirical climatic classification scheme based on mean temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation?
accepted.x: Wladimir Koeppen proposed an empirical climatic classification based on mean temperature and precipitation, with climate types linked to natural vegetation.
accepted.tq: Use the direct name-and-contribution recall method.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the ‘A’ group in Koeppen’s classification?
o: Polar climate with the warmest month below 10°C
Dry climate in which evaporation exceeds precipitation
Cold snow-forest climate with the coldest month below -3°C
Tropical humid climate with the coolest month above 18°C
accepted.x: The A group represents tropical humid climates where the coolest month has a temperature above 18°C.
accepted.tq: Match the group with its defining temperature criterion.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the major groups of Koeppen’s classification:
1. Group B represents dry climates in which evaporation exceeds precipitation.
2. Group C represents warm temperate climates with the coldest month between -3°C and 18°C.
3. Group D represents cold snow-forest climates with the coldest month below -3°C.
4. Group E represents polar climates with the warmest month below 10°C.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the criteria for Koeppen groups B, C, D and E.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical boundary before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: In Koeppen’s classification, the letter ‘H’ denotes:
accepted.x: H denotes a highland climate in which low temperatures are controlled mainly by altitude.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the exact classification letter from similar-sounding alternatives.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in respect of the second letters used in Koeppen’s classification?
accepted.x: The second letter f indicates that there is no dry season. The letters m, w and s indicate monsoon, dry winter and dry summer respectively.
accepted.tq: Use the confusable-pair method for the letters w and s.

accepted.s: The code ‘BWhw’ in the Indian application of Koeppen’s classification represents which region?
o: West Rajasthan and parts of Punjab
The Ganga plain and northern Madhya Pradesh
accepted.x: BWhw is associated with extreme western Rajasthan. BShw covers western Rajasthan, north-west Gujarat and parts of Punjab.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely related BShw and BWhw regional codes.

accepted.s: Which one of the following climatic codes is associated with Arunachal Pradesh?
accepted.x: Arunachal Pradesh is represented by the Dfc climatic code in the given Indian application of Koeppen’s scheme.
accepted.tq: Link the regional location directly with its classification code.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Amw — West coast south of Goa
2. As — Coromandel coast and Tamil Nadu
3. Aw — Most of the peninsular plateau
4. Dfc — Arunachal Pradesh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the Indian regional applications of Koeppen’s classification.
accepted.tq: Verify each code-region pair independently before choosing the complete combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Thornthwaite’s classification from Koeppen’s classification?
o: Thornthwaite used only natural vegetation, whereas Koeppen used only altitude.
Thornthwaite emphasised precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, whereas Koeppen used temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation.
Thornthwaite was based exclusively on pressure, whereas Koeppen was based on winds.
Both classifications used exactly the same criteria and symbols.
accepted.x: Thornthwaite’s scheme is based on precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, including potential evapotranspiration. Koeppen used temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation.
accepted.tq: Identify the reversed-criteria trap in a comparison question.

accepted.s: Thornthwaite first proposed his climatic classification in 1931 and revised it in:
accepted.x: Thornthwaite proposed the classification in 1931 and revised it in 1948.
accepted.tq: Use the date-pair recall method and distinguish the revision year from the original year.

accepted.s: In Thornthwaite’s classification, potential evapotranspiration is used as an indicator of:
accepted.x: Thornthwaite’s classification considers precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, with potential evapotranspiration serving as the basis for thermal efficiency.
accepted.tq: Connect the technical term with the exact classification basis.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its climatic criterion in the classification table?
accepted.x: Group D has the coldest month below -3°C, not above 18°C. The criteria stated for Groups A, B and E are correct.
accepted.tq: Find the one reversed temperature criterion.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an element of climate listed in climatological analysis?
accepted.x: The listed elements of climate are temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, precipitation and cloudiness. Lithology is not an element of climate in this list.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider from the standard set of climatic elements.
accepted.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

accepted.s: Weather is best defined as:
o: The state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time
The long-term distribution of vegetation over a region
The average atmospheric condition over a period of 30 years
The seasonal variation in ocean currents only
accepted.x: Weather refers to the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time. Climate refers to average weather over a long period.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the short-term weather definition from the long-term climate definition.
accepted.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

accepted.s: The World Meteorological Organization’s standard period for describing climate normals is:
accepted.x: The WMO standard describes climate using average weather conditions over a period of 30 years.
accepted.tq: Test the standard numerical period directly.
accepted.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A climograph represents monthly temperature and rainfall of a station on one chart.
2. Temperature is generally represented by a line in a climograph.
3. Rainfall is generally represented by bars in a climograph.
4. A climograph can assist in identifying the climate type of a place.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: A climograph combines monthly temperature, shown by a line, and rainfall, shown by bars, and is used to interpret the climate type of a station.
accepted.tq: Combine the chart components and their use before selecting the coded answer.
accepted.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

accepted.s: The current IMD rainfall normal for the southwest monsoon season, based on the 1971–2020 period, is:
accepted.x: The IMD normal rainfall for June–September, based on the 1971–2020 base period, is 868.6 mm.
accepted.tq: Separate the precise normal value from nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

accepted.s: The IMD rainfall normal of 868.6 mm refers to rainfall during:
accepted.x: The 868.6 mm normal is the long-period average rainfall for the June–September southwest monsoon season.
accepted.tq: Match the numerical normal with its exact reference period.
accepted.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

accepted.s: The current IMD rainfall normal of 868.6 mm is calculated using which base period?
accepted.x: The current IMD normal uses the 1971–2020 base period.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the correct climatological base period from standard alternatives.
accepted.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

accepted.s: Magnetic minerals preserved in the sediments of Bakhira Lake are significant because they provide a record of Indian monsoon variability extending approximately:
accepted.x: Magnetic minerals in Bakhira Lake sediments provide an approximately 25,000-year record of Indian monsoon variability.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive large-number recall technique.

accepted.s: Bakhira Lake, associated with the palaeoclimatic record of Indian monsoon variability, is located in:
accepted.x: Bakhira Lake is in Uttar Pradesh, and its sediments preserve the long-term monsoon record.
accepted.tq: Match the named geographical feature with its state.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about projected coastal climatic conditions is correct?
o: About 40 coastal districts may warm by over 1°C by 2040, with Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu receiving excess southwest-monsoon rain.
About 15 coastal districts may cool by over 1°C by 2040, with Andhra Pradesh receiving deficient monsoon rain.
All coastal districts are projected to warm by exactly 1°C by 2040.
Only inland districts of Andhra Pradesh are projected to experience excess southwest-monsoon rain.
accepted.x: The projection concerns about 40 coastal districts warming by more than 1°C by 2040, while Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu are expected to receive excess southwest-monsoon rain.
accepted.tq: Reject extreme words such as ‘all’ and ‘exactly’ while retaining the precise projection.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the geographical and climatic setting of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It lies between 19°07′ N and 25°41′ N and is classified as E/ET.
It lies between 8°41′ N and 15°07′ N and is classified as Amw.
It lies entirely north of 20° N and is classified as BWhw.
It lies between 12°41′ N and 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, or tropical wet and dry climate.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh extends from 12°41′ N to 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, representing a tropical wet and dry climate.
accepted.tq: Combine latitude limits with the correct Koeppen code and reject reversed ranges.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four climatic regions identified in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The four regions are humid coastal, deltaic, semi-arid Rayalaseema and hill micro-climates. Ladakh is not an Andhra Pradesh climatic region.
accepted.tq: Find the geographically misplaced regional description.

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists only of hill micro-climate locations in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Araku, Lambasingi and Horsley Hills are cited as examples of hill micro-climates in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete location group without an outside place.

accepted.s: According to the recent classification stated for Andhra Pradesh, the State has:
accepted.x: The recent APSES 2024–25 classification identifies six agro-climatic zones in Andhra Pradesh. Older books may state seven.
accepted.tq: Handle the current-versus-older figure distinction carefully.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the number of agro-climatic zones in Andhra Pradesh and India?
o: Andhra Pradesh has fifteen, while India has six.
Andhra Pradesh has four, while India has fifteen.
Andhra Pradesh has six, while India has fifteen.
Both Andhra Pradesh and India have seven.
accepted.x: The current figures stated are six agro-climatic zones for Andhra Pradesh and fifteen for India.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of comparison to avoid interchanging state and national figures.

accepted.s: The recent listing of Andhra Pradesh’s six agro-climatic zones is arranged with reference to:
o: The four major climatic regions of the world
accepted.x: The APSES 2024–25 table lists the six agro-climatic zones against the 13 pre-2022 districts.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative framework attached to the classification.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the year 2025 and La Niña is correct?
o: 2025 was the first year without any ocean warming.
2025 had no association with La Niña conditions.
2025 was the warmest La Niña year on record.
2025 was the coldest La Niña year on record.
accepted.x: The stated current-affairs fact is that 2025 was the warmest La Niña year on record.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute reversals of the reported climate record.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the global ocean climate in 2025:
1. Oceans held more than 90% of the excess heat.
2. Approximately 90% of the ocean surface experienced marine heatwaves.
3. Less than 10% of the excess heat was held by the oceans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the oceans held more than 90%, not less than 10%, of the excess heat.
accepted.tq: Spot the numerical reversal in the false statement.
